stem: In a patient with polyarticular JIA, a positive Rheumatoid Factor (RF) typically indicates:

options.text: A more destructive disease course and poorer outcome
A high likelihood of spontaneous remission
That the child has systemic juvenile arthritis
A milder form of the disease requiring less treatment

explanation: RF-positive polyarticular JIA essentially parallels adult rheumatoid arthritis, which is aggressive and requires very early immunosuppression.
rationale: Think about the severity of 'adult-type' rheumatoid arthritis when it starts in childhood.

optionExplanations.A: RF-positive polyarticular JIA essentially parallels adult rheumatoid arthritis, which is aggressive and requires very early immunosuppression.
optionExplanations.B: RF-positive patients have very low remission rates and often face a lifelong disease course.
optionExplanations.C: Systemic JIA is a distinct subtype and is not defined by Rheumatoid Factor positivity.
optionExplanations.D: RF-positive disease is destructive and deforming, necessitating aggressive rather than mild treatment.

source.hint: Think about the severity of 'adult-type' rheumatoid arthritis when it starts in childhood.
